subject: Mathematics
title: Count and Arrange
subtitle: Counting, comparing and arranging
hero_picture: A Kerala primary school with a red-tiled roof, yellow school buses, children walking in with their parents, green trees around.

sections.heading: Count the things
text: Anvith and friends put things in rows.
Pencils are the most. The sharpener is the least.
sections.caption: Counting school things
sections.picture: A table with school things laid out in rows to count: 5 pencils, 3 erasers, 4 rulers and 1 sharpener.

sections.heading: Vehicles at school
text: There was a meeting at Anvith's school.
They counted cars, autos, bicycles and scooters.
Which vehicle is more? Which is less?
sections.caption: Vehicles outside school
sections.picture: Vehicles parked outside a school: some cars, auto-rickshaws, bicycles, scooters and one bus, clearly countable.

sections.heading: Toys on the shelf
text: They counted the toys in the pre-primary class.
Cars, balls, bats, teddy bears and flowers.
Are there more bats than balls?
sections.caption: Toys on the shelf
sections.picture: A pre-primary classroom shelf with toys to count: toy cars, balls, bats, teddy bears and flowers.

sections.heading: Arrange in order
text: Start with the most, end with the least.
Now we can see at once which is more!
sections.caption: Toys in order
sections.picture: Children arranging their toys in neat rows from the most to the least on a classroom floor.

sections.heading: Line up in order
text: We can arrange people and things in order.
sections.caption: A line from short to tall
sections.picture: A smiling teacher and children standing in a line in order of height, shortest to tallest, in a school yard.

rhyme: Count the pencils, one, two, three,
Count the erasers, look and see,
Which has more and which has less?
Put them in order, no more guess!
activity: Count the spoons, plates and cups in your kitchen. Which is the most? Which is the least?
talk: What was the most on Anvith's table?
Are there more chairs or more tables in your class?
summary: We count, compare and arrange things to see which is more and which is less.

questions.prompt: 5 pencils and 3 erasers. Which is more?
4 rulers and 1 sharpener. How many more rulers?
3 teddy bears and 3 cars. What can we say?
